title: feat(motion,app): Trochoidal slot - engagement-controlled trochoid operation (#220 slice 1)
body:
Slice 1 of #220: an engagement-controlled trochoid generator and a standalone **Trochoidal slot** operation. Branched from upstream/main; the fork is synced at v0.15.0.

## What changed
**The generator** (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/trochoid_slot.rs`, `trochoid_loops.rs`, `trochoid_air.rs`), specced from Otkur & Lazoglu 2007 and Rauch, Duc & Hascoet 2009.
- **Loop shape:** each loop is the front arc of a circle of radius ρ = B / cos 10°, with B = (W − D)/2 by default. The arc runs wall to wall and meets each wall at 10°.
  - On a straight chain the loops are shifted copies, so they never cross. Classic full-circle trochoids always cross the previous loop, and the verifier holds the post on a same-depth crossing.
  - A wall move between arcs cleans the cusp, and a fillet (the smoothing radius) blends it into each arc.
- **Start and end:** a helical bore of radius B at the start. A stepped fan of arcs closes the far end.
- **Returns:** microlift (default 0.3 mm, retracing the arc just cut at the return feed) or retract.
- **Engagement:** measured with the Adaptive pins' dexel yardstick (`quality::measure`) on each candidate level. The planner tries steps from 100% of the user's step down to 7%, and a note says when the step was cut. Adaptive's planner raster was not reused because it counts finished walls as contact (see the decision file).
- **Lifted returns over air:** a new `machining2d::lifted_cut` checks each lifted return against the in-process stock.
- **Refused by name:**
  - a channel narrower than the tool (it suggests a plain Slot);
  - a loop wider than the room;
  - a limit no step can hold (the message gives the lowest reading, where it was, and at which step);
  - a loop leaving the channel;
  - a crossing (the verifier's own `crossed_pairs`);
  - a lifted return over stock.

**The operation:** `OpType::TrochoidalSlot` (kind 39) in the ribbon's 2D mill family.
- **Authoring:** two endpoints and a width, like Slot, verified against the slot's stadium.
- **Parameters:** loop width (auto), forward step, max engagement, return, microlift height, smoothing radius, stock to leave, heights, stepdown, cutting/return/plunge feeds, climb.
- **Undo and editing:** create and edit are undoable (`CreateOperation` / `EditOperationParams`). It has a small Geometry/Heights/Passes/Feeds page.
- **Project file:** a `trochoidal_slot` params entry. There is no `PROJECT_VERSION` bump, following the probe op's precedent (#108/#344) for an appended kind. Older builds won't read a document that uses the new kind.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/220-trochoidal-slot.md`.

## How tested
- **motion `trochoid_slot`** (7 tests, plus 2 unit tests):
  - A full-width slot (D10 in W16, 1 mm step) measures θmax **66.5°**; a straight Slot in the same channel measures **180°**.
  - A 60° limit forces the step down, and the note says so.
  - The verifier is clean (no crossing, gouge or rapid-in-stock) for climb and conventional, microlift and retract.
  - Microlift returns land on air, and the check catches one placed over stock.
  - Named refusals; the loops post as arcs.
- **app `trochoid_op`:** create and edit undo/redo; generate verifies clean and posts G03; a too-narrow channel is refused by name; project round trip.
- **New goldens:** `golden/trochoid_slot_small.cl` and `golden/nc/trochoid_slot_small.nc` (Fanuc, G02/G03).
- **Edited tests:** `ribbon` and `probe_op` pinned the probe as the last kind; they now pin index 38, and kind 39 is pinned.
- **Passing:**
  - motion `adaptive_band`;
  - app mill2d_b/c, ribbon, tool_law, probe_op, golden_cl, fanuc_post, project_roundtrip, operations, commands_undo, conformance, heidenhain_block_form, slot_caps, drill_prior_kinds, pick_doors, setup_align, wall_column_gouge, drilling_axial;
  - ui kind/ribbon/tab tests (including `every_registry_kind_gets_its_tab_bar`) and ui `operations`;
  - clippy on motion, app and ui (`-D warnings`).
- **Runtime:** the `trochoid_slot` binary takes about 80 s in debug when run in parallel. Each test is under 25 s alone.

## Not exercised (draft)
- **No run yet:** a GUI hands-on check, and a Hub or machine run of the posted arcs. This adds new posted G-code.
- **Deferred to later slices:** Adaptive's trochoidal mode (Done means 2), the corner-overload pin, centre-line picking from a model chain (typed endpoints today), the in-plane cutting return, feed reduction where engagement rises, and wall finishing when the loop band is narrower than the room.

Changelog: Trochoidal slot operation: an engagement-controlled trochoid along a typed centre line - measured contact angle held under a limit by adapting the step, microlift or retract returns, named refusals (#220, slice 1)

Refs #220

title: feat(ui): Machines pane "Use for this setup" assigns the selected machine
body:
**Replaces #426** (opened from the old fork, which can no longer take pushes). Same head commit; nothing else changed.

**Stacked on #382** (Machines pane, browse + validate): this branch carries #382's commits plus a merge of current main. Merge #382 first; this PR's own diff is then the last two commits (`cb293f30`, `35cfa074`) plus the merge.

## What changed
- The Machines pane's detail view gets a **"Use for this setup"** button under the validation verdict. Clicking it queues `CommandKind::UseCatalogueMachine(MachineSource)`.
- It follows main's per-setup machine route (#343): `State::mount_catalogue` -> `route_machine(MachineVerb::Mount(..))`. If the active setup owns its machine, the selected machine replaces it (`SetSetupMachine`); otherwise the document's machine changes (`LoadMachine`). One undo step either way.
- Validation is re-run at assignment: `machine::library::read_for_assign` re-reads the built-in text or file, runs `validate_text`, and refuses with the first refusal, so a refused machine never mounts even if the command is queued directly. Shared by `LoadMachine::from_catalogue`, the new `SetSetupMachine::from_catalogue` and the UI route.
- The button is disabled with the reason shown under it and on hover: "fails validation - <first refusal> (and N more)" or "it is already this setup's machine" (reads `machine::of`, the active setup's effective machine).
- `MachineSource::mount_path()` mounts built-ins at `built-in: <name>`, the path the Setup pane's Library list already uses.
- Decision only (no code): the `machine_editor.rs` window becomes the pane's edit mode when the editing slice (#383) lands.

## Readings
Debug, M5 Mac. `scripts/gate.sh quick` (all camcraft-app + camcraft-ui suites): 1734 passed, 4 failed - all known reds on main (`setup_stock_source::a_new_block_after_a_flip…` #415; GPU headless trio). Clippy `-D warnings` clean on app + ui.

## Pinning tests
- App `crates/app/tests/machine_assign.rs`: `assigning_a_catalogue_machine_does_undoes_and_redoes`, `a_refused_machine_cannot_be_assigned_and_says_why`, `a_setup_with_its_own_machine_takes_the_catalogue_machine`.
- UI lib `egui_app::tests::machines_pane`: `use_for_this_setup_assigns_the_selected_machine_and_undo_restores_it`, `a_refused_machine_cannot_be_assigned_and_names_why`, `use_for_this_setup_replaces_an_own_machine_and_leaves_the_document_alone`.

## Not exercised
No hand GUI run yet (**draft until the GUI check**); Ctrl+Y redo only at app level; disabled-hover text not asserted. Posted G-code unchanged (machines mount through the existing commands).

Decisions: `docs/decisions/384-machines-use-for-setup.md`.

Changelog: The Machines pane's "Use for this setup" assigns the selected machine to the active setup (its own machine or the document's), undoable; a machine that fails validation can't be assigned and says why

Fixes #384

title: feat(ui): preview the incoming stock in the viewport on the setup page
body:
**Replaces #429** (opened from the old fork, which can no longer take pushes). Same head commit; nothing else changed.

## What changed
While a setup's settings page is open and its stock source is "What <previous setup> leaves behind", the viewport draws the incoming body as a translucent **teal** sheet, in the active setup's frame, distinct from the setup's own Stock node.

- App: new `setup_stock_view::incoming_shape(world, setup)` calls `stock_sim::incoming_body` once and returns the box/volume plus `body.display().surface(&[])` as triangles mapped into the viewport's frame (`A_active * inverse(A_setup)`; identity when the setup is active). An empty body or sheet is an error naming the setup; a bad index is skipped, never a panic.
- UI: `incoming_view::IncomingView` caches it keyed by (setup, active setup, `doc_version`) - measured once per document version, never per frame - refreshed at the end of `drain_actions` and cleared the moment the page closes, another page opens, or the setup switches to its own stock. A failed measurement is logged once and draws nothing.
- Drawing: `collect_parts` adds a stock-type part with vertex class 4; `fs_stock` paints class 4 as teal rgb (0.12, 0.66, 0.74) at alpha 0.45 in the existing translucent stock pass.
- The page's incoming box/volume text reuses the viewport's measurement, so there is one program sim per version instead of two.
- Display only: no command, nothing undoable (ephemeral view state per AGENTS.md). No files #412 touches were edited (`stock_sim*.rs`, `operation/*`, `rest/*`).

## Readings
Debug, M5 Mac. `scripts/gate.sh quick` (camcraft-app + camcraft-ui suites): 1718 passed, 4 failed - all known reds on main (`setup_stock_source::a_new_block_after_a_flip…` #415; GPU headless trio). Clippy `-D warnings` clean. The changed WGSL shader was validated offline with naga 30.0.1; the `gpu_render` tests skip here (no adapter in the sandbox).

## Pinning tests
- UI lib `egui_app::incoming_view_tests`: `the_incoming_stock_shows_while_the_carried_setups_page_is_open` (real properties pane via egui_kittest: one class-4 part with Setup2's page open, top at Z 16 where Setup1 faced to; measured once, three more frames measure nothing, a `doc_version` bump measures once more; Close removes it), `no_incoming_stock_for_own_stock_or_another_page`.
- App `crates/app/tests/setup_stock_view.rs`: `the_sheet_stands_in_the_active_setups_frame`, `the_first_setup_draws_its_own_block_and_an_unknown_setup_is_named`.

## Not exercised
No real-GPU render of the teal and no hand GUI run yet - **draft until the GUI check**. Known limit: the traced whole-program stock view replaces all stock-type parts, so the overlay hides with it. Posted G-code unchanged.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/406-incoming-stock-preview.md`.

Changelog: The setup page previews the incoming (carried) stock in the viewport as a translucent teal body while a setup that takes what the previous setup leaves behind is open

Fixes #406

title: fix(post): G76 words state the thread passes that were verified
body:
**Replaces #433** (opened from the old fork, which can no longer take pushes). Same head commit; nothing else changed.

**Stacked on #432 (#416).** Part of #363.

## What changed
**With the G76 cycle post option, the G76 words now describe the passes the verdict judged.**
- The record maps 1:1: `G76 P(m)(r)(a) Q(dmin) R(d)` / `G76 X Z P(k) Q(dd) F`, where:
  - dd = the first pass's depth;
  - dmin = the step (constant depth) or the plan's minimum (constant area);
  - d = the finishing pass's own depth;
  - m = 1 + spring passes;
  - a = twice the flank angle.
- **Control model** (GSK988TA, Fanuc-compatible G76):
  - each roughing pass goes to `max(dd·√n, previous + dmin)`, up to k − d;
  - the first finishing pass cuts d, and m − 1 more repeat at k;
  - each pass starts `depth·tan(a/2)` along Z.
- **Refused by name with G76 chosen:** alternating infeed (the CL carries a new `alternating` flag; `ALT 1` is written to the stream only when set), a doubled angle outside 0/29/30/55/60/80 (so 29.5° is refused), and a one-pass thread.

**⚠ This changes posted output for the default G76 thread: `R0` becomes `R0.4`.** The golden `fanuc-lathe/thread_g76.nc` changes on one line: `G76 P010000 Q400 R0` → `G76 P010000 Q400 R0.4`.
- Why: with `R0` the control roughs 0.4, 0.8 and 1.2, then cuts its finishing pass at the root again. That is a fourth full-depth pass the verdict never judged. It's not a gouge, but it isn't what was verified.
- With `R0.4` it roughs 0.4 and 0.8 and finishes at 1.2: exactly the three passes we judge.
- Making `R0` true instead would have meant changing G32 output and the judged passes.
- Note: the #363 research said Q = infeed made the control cut a decreasing ladder. That isn't so, because dmin = infeed clamps every step equal. The real gap was R.

`docs/decisions/417-g76-matches-verified.md`

## How tested
- New app `lathe_post_g76_schedule` (4 tests):
  - a new flank, constant-area golden `thread_g76_area.nc` (`G76 P020055 Q100 R0.05` / `G76 X9.6 Z14 P1200 Q400 F2`): the control's schedule computed from the posted words matches the laid depths and stations within 1 µm;
  - the default (`R0.4`) and a 0.5 step (`Q500 R0.2`) also match;
  - one refusal per unexpressible option;
  - `ALT` survives the stream and the project file.
- Existing post, cl, inverted_post, lathe_post, golden_cl, project_roundtrip, tool_law, tool_gate and commands_undo suites are green.
- `clippy --tests -D warnings` (cl, post, motion, app, ui) is clean.
- The gate escalated to batch (cl changed). It fails only on tests already red on main: headless GPU, #415, and `swarf_pose_continuity` (PR #351).

## Not exercised / not confirmed by sources (draft until a lathe sim or machine run)
1. Which way Fanuc shifts Z per pass for flank infeed. This follows LinuxCNC's sign; either sign is gouge-safe.
2. Whether the control also shifts each pass's end Z. If not, early passes end up to k·tan θ off at the runout, shallower than the root.
3. How the minimum-depth clamp applies (read as a per-pass minimum, per the manual's definition).
4. Micron rounding of the words: the control's ladder can differ by under 1 µm.

None of these moves the finished thread form.

Changelog: G76 threading output states the passes that were verified: the finish allowance R is posted (default threads now post R0.4 instead of R0), and options G76 cannot express are refused by name (#417)

Fixes #417

title: feat(turning): threading infeed method and decreasing-depth pass schedule
body:
**Replaces #432** (opened from the old fork, which can no longer take pushes). Same head commit; nothing else changed.

Part of #363 (peck threading; the research comment there has the sources). Follow-up #417 (PR stacked on this one) makes the G76 output match these passes.

## What changed
**New threading op param `infeed_plan` (`turning::ThreadInfeed`).**
- **Infeed method:** radial, modified flank at an angle θ, or alternating flank.
- **Depth schedule:** constant depth, or constant area (first depth × √n).
- **Minimum depth per pass, finish allowance, and spring passes** (default 0, capped at 98).
- The existing `infeed` is the first-pass depth.
- It's shown as rows on the op's Passes tab (`thread_infeed_page.rs`).

**Kernel.** `crates/motion/src/turning/infeed.rs` lays the passes from the plan. `thread_in` calls `thread_planned_in` with the default plan.
- **Flank:** each pass starts shifted by −(tip − root)·tan θ along its travel. Finishing and spring passes sit on the pitch lattice, so lead and spindle phase never change.
- **Safety:** every pass stays inside the finished V exactly when θ ≤ half the insert's included angle. A larger angle is refused by name at the command (create, paste, edit, retype via `thread_gate`) and again at Generate.
- **Alternating:** flips the side each pass.

**The verdict judges the laid passes.** `the_verdict_reads_the_shifted_pass` pins a past-half-angle pass being convicted. `attach_cycle` moved to `thread_cycle.rs`.

**Defaults are byte-identical.** The default plan makes the same `blade::rungs(root, ref_top, infeed, 0)` call at the same stations.
- The op stamp includes the plan only when it isn't the default, so cached threads stay fresh.
- The project key is written only when non-default, so there's no version rung. An older build drops a non-default plan and cuts the radial ladder; that's not a gouge.
- No existing golden changed.

`docs/decisions/416-thread-infeed.md`

## How tested
- New motion `turning_thread_infeed` (8 tests):
  - √n depths with the minimum-depth clamp;
  - allowance plus spring-pass count;
  - flank shift, including the full 30°;
  - alternating flip;
  - verdict silent for every method × schedule on the thread fixture;
  - a shifted pass is convicted;
  - refusals by name.
- New app `turning_thread_infeed` (4/4, plus 1 after the merge): the plan runs in a document; refusals at create and edit; undo/redo (op goes stale); project round-trip with no key for the default plan.
- Existing suites unchanged and green: motion `turning_thread` and `turning_thread_cycle`; app `turning_thread`, `lathe_post_g76`, `lathe_field_tools` and `project_roundtrip`.
- `clippy --tests -D warnings` is clean.
- `scripts/gate.sh quick` passes except tests that already fail on main:
  - the headless-GPU ui tests;
  - `setup_stock_source::a_new_block_after_a_flip…` (#415);
  - `swarf_pose_continuity` (2 tests; red on main, fixed by PR #351).

## Not exercised (draft)
- GUI check of the new Passes-tab rows.
- **Posted G-code for non-default plans** (flank, constant area, allowance, spring passes) is new. It needs a lathe simulator or machine run before ready. Default plans post exactly as before.

Changelog: Threading op: infeed method (radial / modified flank / alternating), decreasing-depth schedule, minimum depth, finish allowance and spring passes (#416)

Fixes #416

title: feat(setup): per-setup post options and the setup's own tool-list export
body:
> Replaces #423, moved to the new fork (the old fork left NeoTech's network, and a push there closes the PR). Main is merged in. The two conflicts were module lists in `ui/src/state.rs` and `egui_app/tests.rs`, where both sides are kept (#371's tool_body). `setup_post_options` passes 8/8, the ui lib tests 11/11, and clippy for app and ui is clean. Still a draft, waiting on the hands-on GUI check (rebuilt `camcraft-ui-423`).

## What changed
**Post options per setup** (same own / follow-the-document law #343 gave the post itself):
- `SetupDef.post_options: Option<PostOptions>`; `None` follows the document (every older file and every new setup).
- New undoable command `SetSetupPostOptions`; a no-op request is refused by name. A datum transfer copies the source setup's options with its post.
- `posting::post_options` returns the active setup's own options, else the document's (mirrors `post_of`). "Skip pauses and homes" is read per operation from that op's setup, so one setup can skip its stops while another keeps them. Output (one file per op) and thread output are program-wide: setups that disagree are refused by name, next to #343's one-mount check.
- Project file: an additive setup key `post_options` (`{"threading":"g32"|"g76","skip_stops":..,"per_op_files":..}`), omitted when `None`; no version step (stays v57), so a document that never sets it saves byte-identically. An unknown threading word is a corrupt-file refusal naming the setup.
- UI: the setup's **Post** page ends with a "Post options" group - radios "Use the document's post options" / "This setup has its own post options" and a note saying whose options the widgets above edit. The existing option widgets route to the active setup's own options when it has them.

**Setup tool-list export**
- `app::tool_list_export` (pure read): rows in first-use order from `tool_list::for_setup` - T number, name, diameter (mm), kind, holder (`D x L` or `none`), ops using it. `.csv` -> RFC 4180 CSV (CRLF, quoted fields); any other extension -> fixed-column text.
- The setup's **Tool list** page gets an "Export tool list…" button (save dialog, CSV/Text filters, default `<Setup>-tools.csv`). A command-free file write like the setup sheet: nothing enters the history.

## Readings
Debug, M5 Mac. `scripts/gate.sh quick` (all camcraft-app + camcraft-ui suites): 1725 passed, 4 failed - all known reds on main: `setup_stock_source::a_new_block_after_a_flip…` (#415) and the GPU headless trio (`headless_run_succeeds`, `headless_cli_exit_code_is_zero`, `egui_headless_cli_exit_code_is_zero`). Goldens (`golden_cl` 23, posts) and `project_roundtrip` (69) unchanged. Clippy `-D warnings` clean on app + ui.

## Pinning tests
- App `crates/app/tests/setup_post_options.rs`: `a_setups_own_post_options_do_undo_redo`, `a_setup_that_skips_posts_without_its_stops_while_the_other_follows_the_document`, `setups_disagreeing_on_the_output_are_refused_by_name`, `a_single_setup_document_posts_byte_identically`, `own_post_options_round_trip_and_old_files_follow_the_document`, `a_datum_transfer_keeps_the_source_setups_post_options`, `the_tool_list_exports_as_csv_and_text`, `a_tool_list_field_with_a_comma_is_quoted`.
- UI lib `egui_app::tests::setup_post_options`: `the_option_switches_land_on_the_active_setups_own_options`, `the_post_page_radio_gives_the_setup_its_own_options`, `the_tool_list_page_exports_the_setups_tools`.

## Not exercised
The real rfd save dialog (tests write through `ToolListExportFile`); a per-setup G76 thread post end to end on Fanuc Lathe; one-file-per-op from a setup's own options (same `post_options` path `per_op_files` already covers). No hand GUI check yet - **draft until the GUI check**.

Posted G-code: existing documents post byte-identically; output only differs for a setup that is given its own options.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/389-setup-tool-list.md`.

title: feat(app): recognise pockets and slots and turn them into operations
body:
## What changed

Pocket and slot recognition, headless (app layer and MCP; no GUI changes).

- **`camcraft_app::recognize`** (new module: `mod`, `walls`, `shape`, `op`):
  - `pockets_of(world, model)` reads the model's planar-face topology (`geometry::feature`, the same B-rep `list_features` and the pick tools use).
  - A level, up-facing face is a **floor** when the facets across its outer ring rise from it and lean into it (a concave edge), and those walls face each other across the floor.
  - Walled all round, it is a **closed pocket**. With wall-less spans it is an **open pocket**. A straight channel (at least 2 widths long, both long sides walled, each end wholly walled or wholly open, area within 3% of the shape) is a **slot**, with each end open, round or square.
  - Each result carries:
    - the outer ring (world XY, counter-clockwise), island count and area;
    - floor Z, top Z (highest wall point) and depth;
    - the **tightest inside corner radius** (0 = sharp, `None` where no two walls meet) and the **open spans**;
    - for a slot: centreline ends, **width**, length and end kinds.
  - Shoulders, corner steps, top faces and a plate around a boss are not pockets.
- **`recognize::operation_for`** maps a feature onto `CreateOperation`'s inputs, so creating it is one undoable History step with every field editable:
  - a pocket (or a slot with a square closed end, which a round cap would leave standing) becomes a **2D Pocket** on a pick of the floor face, with `bottom_z` at the selection bottom and `top_z` at the selection bottom + depth;
  - a slot with round or open ends becomes a **Slot** along its centreline: width, fixed heights, source stock, open ends running full width out to the floor's edge.
- **MCP `detect_pockets {model, create?, tool?, name?}`** lists the features, each with the floor's `face:0x…` id (the id `list_features` prints) and the operation kind it would create. With `create` it adds that operation, one undo step.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/35-pocket-slot-recognition.md`.

Provenance: the concave-edge depression rule follows Joshi & Chang (CAD 20(2), 1988). The minimum-area rectangle follows Freeman & Shapira (CACM 18(7), 1975). No vendor material was consulted.

## How tested

Quick gate, debug: `pocket_recognition` 10/10, `mcp_pockets` 3/3, `mcp` 13/13, `mcp_pick` 7/7, `mcp_setup` 18/18, `cli` 2/2, `feature` 3/3. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

Pinning tests, on watertight meshes built in code (`crates/app/tests/pocket_support`):
- `a_rectangular_pocket_is_closed_with_sharp_corners`
- `a_pocket_with_corner_radii_reports_its_tightest_corner` (r 4)
- `a_round_ended_closed_slot_is_a_slot_between_its_cap_centres`
- `a_through_slot_is_open_at_both_ends`
- `an_open_slot_with_a_square_end_machines_as_a_pocket`
- `parts_without_pockets_list_none` (plain block, shoulder, corner step, boss)
- `degenerate_input_refuses_cleanly` (unknown model; NaN, infinite and zero-area facets; a torn half mesh)
- `a_recognised_pocket_becomes_an_undoable_pocket_that_cuts_to_its_floor`: generates with no Gouge, reaches the floor, stays inside the ring; undo removes it
- `an_open_slot_machined_as_a_pocket_cuts_its_floor_without_a_gouge`
- `a_recognised_slot_becomes_a_slot_cut_along_its_centreline`: checks the path geometry exactly; undo removes it
- MCP: `detect_pockets_lists_a_rounded_pocket_and_creates_its_pocket` (generate + verify ok; undo/redo), `detect_pockets_creates_a_slot_for_a_through_slot`, `detect_pockets_refuses_bad_arguments_by_name`

## Not exercised / known gaps

- **#510 (filed):** every typed Slot whose cutter rides its round cap is reported as a gouge today, recognised or not. The likely cause is the stadium region's chorded caps measured against `GOUGE_TOL`. Until #510 lands, a recognised slot's Slot op refuses to post. Its test checks the path geometry, not the verifier's verdict.
- **Not recognised:**
  - through pockets / windows (no floor face);
  - non-level floors and tilted setup frames (the read is world +Z);
  - curved slots, T-slots and undercuts.
  - Each level of a stepped pocket is its own feature.
- An open pocket's open side is not written into the area controls' open boundary. The tool's corner radius stays uncut where a wall meets an open edge.
- **GUI entry point:** #511. Not exercised on real STEP parts or by hand. The release-tier heavy lanes were not run.

Changelog: Pocket and slot recognition - `detect_pockets` (MCP) lists a model's closed/open pockets and slots (depth, corner radius, slot width, open sides) and creates the Pocket or Slot that machines one, one undo step (#35)

title: feat(mcp): serve the MCP tool table live from inside the GUI
body:
> Replaces #428, moved to the new fork (the old one left NeoTech's network; a push there closes the PR). Main is merged in; the one conflict was the module list in `mcp/mod.rs`, where both sides are kept. `mcp` 9/9, `mcp_live` 6/6 and `mcp_pick` 2/2 pass, and clippy for app and ui is clean. Still a draft, waiting on the hands-on GUI check (refreshed binaries `camcraft-ui-428` and `camcraft-cli-428`).

## What changed
The GUI can host the same MCP tool table (`app::mcp`) live, so an agent drives the open document and the user watches it in the viewport.

- **Opt-in, loopback only.** Off by default; started with `--mcp-port <n>` / `--mcp-port=<n>` or `CAMCRAFT_MCP_PORT` (flag wins; `0` picks a free port). Binds 127.0.0.1. A bad value exits 2.
- **Transport:** plain TCP carrying the same newline-delimited JSON-RPC as `camcraft-cli mcp`, plus a stdio<->TCP bridge `camcraft-cli mcp --connect <host:port>` so stdio MCP clients can attach.
- **Threading:** a std listener thread (one client at a time) only moves text; each line goes over an mpsc channel to the UI thread with its own reply channel and wakes the idle winit loop (`EventLoopProxy`). No world access off the UI thread.
- **Same document, same History.** The UI thread answers in `State::drain_actions` after the user's own queued commands, through the existing `Server` dispatch (no tool code duplicated): the `Env` gets the GUI's world handle and borrows the GUI's own `History` for the call. An agent step is one Ctrl+Z, and the agent's `undo`/`redo` walk the user's steps too. Every call bumps `doc_version`; the status line reads `agent: <tool>`.
- **Status strip** shows `MCP listening on 127.0.0.1:<port>` while the server runs (default frames unchanged).
- **Never crash:** malformed JSON -> -32700; a dropped client, closed channel or >16 MiB line is logged and the listener carries on; dropping the `Inbox` stops and joins the thread (~50 ms) at shutdown.
- **Refused live:** `open_project` (would replace the user's document past the unsaved-changes prompt).
- New code: `crates/app/src/mcp/{listen,live,bridge}.rs`, `crates/ui/src/mcp_host.rs`; `mcp/tools.rs` and `mcp/edit.rs` untouched.

## Maintainer note (judgement call)
There is no authentication: any local process can drive the open document while the server is on. Being off by default and loopback-only is the guard; a token could be added later if wanted. `save_project` without a path saves over the open project but does not mark it clean, so the app may still ask to save. A long `generate` blocks the UI frame for its duration.

## Readings
Debug, M5 Mac. `scripts/gate.sh quick` (camcraft-app + camcraft-ui suites): 1722 passed, 4 failed - all known reds on main (`setup_stock_source::a_new_block_after_a_flip…` #415; GPU headless trio). Clippy `-D warnings` clean. Hand run: `camcraft-ui --mcp-port 7333` driven through `camcraft-cli mcp --connect` (set_stock, add_tool, add_operation all `isError:false`; `get_job` over nc showed the op in the app's world).

## Pinning tests
- App `crates/app/tests/mcp_live.rs`: `a_live_call_lands_on_the_callers_history_and_its_undo_reverts_it`, `each_agent_step_is_one_undo_step_on_the_shared_history`, `the_live_session_refuses_open_project_and_reads_bad_lines_as_errors`, `the_port_flag_is_opt_in_and_checked`, `a_loopback_client_drives_the_owners_document_and_survives_bad_input` (real loopback TCP), `the_bridge_copies_stdio_to_a_live_session_and_back`.
- UI lib `egui_app::tests::mcp_live`: `an_agents_operation_shows_in_the_browser_and_ctrl_z_removes_it`, `the_status_strip_says_the_server_is_listening`.

## Not exercised
Ctrl+Z pressed by hand in the real window (harness only) - **draft until the GUI check**; Windows/Linux runs (std::net only); a real MCP client app beyond the bridge/nc; the bind-failure path (port in use). Posted G-code unchanged.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/183-mcp-live-gui.md`.

Changelog: The GUI can serve MCP live on a loopback port (`--mcp-port` / `CAMCRAFT_MCP_PORT`), so an agent's steps land in the open document and Ctrl+Z undoes them; `camcraft-cli mcp --connect` bridges stdio clients

Fixes #183

title: fix(post): judge the tool-number clash per machine
body:
**Replaces #440**, which was opened from the old fork. GitHub detached that fork from this repo's network when NeoTech/Camcraft was briefly private, so #440 can no longer be updated. **Now stacked on #471** (the replacement for #439).

(Originally stacked on #439.) The #438 work is 9d9ac93d.

## What changed
- **The tool-number clash check (#221) is judged per machine.** `tool_numbers::clash_per_machine` runs the existing `clash()` on each machine group from `program_mounts(world, false)`. `posting::op_streams` calls it, which covers per-op files too.
- **Why per machine, not per NC file:** a T number names a pocket in one machine's tool changer.
  - Two machines have two tool tables, so T2 on each is fine.
  - Two posts on one machine still load from one carousel, so a shared number there is still refused.
  - Grouping per file (machine plus post) would let that real clash through, so I rejected it.
- **Messages:** a single-machine program gets the exact #221 message, unchanged. A multi-machine refusal starts with the mount's label (`Setup1 (machine, post): tools '…' and '…' would both post as T3 …`).
- The rationale is in `docs/decisions/388-per-setup-mount.md` (#438 section).

## How tested
- New `setup_mounts_post::a_tool_number_shared_across_machines_posts_but_clashes_within_one`:
  - across machines: a mill tool numbered 2 and the lathe's T2 post as two files;
  - within one machine: a clash is refused, naming both tools, the T number and Setup1, and not the lathe tool.
- `tool_numbers::two_tools_posting_one_number_refuse_by_name` (single machine) is unchanged and passes.
- `setup_mounts_post` 6/6, `setup_mount` 6/6, `tool_numbers` 6/6, `posting` 17/17, `post_not_judged` 4/4. `clippy -p camcraft-app --tests -D warnings` is clean.

Changelog: The tool-number clash is judged per machine, so two machines in one program may each use the same T number (#438)

Fixes #438
